content:
Today Apple launched the latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models. At the same time, the company's various Magic Keyboard accessories have also received a small update.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels on the keys and uses icons instead.

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio are equipped with brand-new chips, including the next-generation M6 and high-end M5 Ultra, delivering a significant boost in performance.

You can now pre-order the latest models: Mac mini here, Mac Studio here.

In addition to the desktop computer upgrades, Apple has also updated the Magic Keyboard lineup, with the new models featuring a subtle change.

The latest Magic Keyboard has removed the text labels on several keys, replacing them with icon symbols.

Apple previously adopted the same approach on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro, and now the Magic Keyboard has received the same modification.

This change applies to all new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: US$99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: US$149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: US$179

Frequently used keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift, and Delete have all had their text removed, displaying only icons. On the extended model with a numeric keypad, keys such as Home, Page Up, and Page Down have also been replaced with new icons in place of the original text.

Apart from the switch to icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks identical to the previous generation in every other respect, still supporting USB-C, with the same features and layout unchanged.

If you would like to order the new Magic Keyboard through Amazon rather than Apple, you can purchase them here: Magic Keyboard, Touch ID version, Touch ID and Numeric Keypad version (in black).

What do you think about the move to abandon text labels on the keys? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
